quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
A hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road safely and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road safely and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights or siren, move as far right as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When can you use hand and arm signals instead of turn signals?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
When your vehicle is loaded and blocks hand signals.
When visibility is low.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day.
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals during the day instead of turn signals. Do not use hand signals at night or when your vehicle is loaded so that others cannot see them.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What are highway signs called that require drivers to obey them?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking these rules can result in penalties.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and slow down.
Honk, steer right, and slow down.
Stay in your lane, honk, and slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and slow down.
questions.explanation: First, honk to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right. Steering left is dangerous because the other driver may correct at the last moment and still hit you. Always slow down firmly and steadily to reduce the impact.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a yellow traffic light.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow light. Slow down and prepare to stop when you see it.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you must stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then go when clear?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always demand the right-of-way in a crosswalk over vehicles.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: A fire engine is following your vehicle on a two-lane street, but it is not using emergency signals. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Speed up to move out of the way.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is behind you but has no siren or flashing lights on, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and you must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and you must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end. Traffic in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: A stopped school bus is on the opposite side of a multilane highway with a median. What must drivers do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the flashing lights to turn off.
Stop until the school bus starts moving.
Stop until the stop arm is raised.
You may drive on.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive on.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median, you can continue driving. You only need to stop if there is no median or divider between the lanes.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a crosswalk.

options.text: 40 feet
20 feet
10 feet
5 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. This keeps the crosswalk visible from both directions.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to show drivers which lanes to use for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes are used for turning or driving straight.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Turn on your signal, find an opening, speed up to match traffic speed, and merge into the opening.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: After one hour or more of rain.
The day after it rains.
In the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in an alley if no sign is posted?

options.text: 35 mph
25 mph
15 mph
10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in an alley is 10 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs that show a different speed.

questions.question: Airbags protect you completely during a crash.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Airbags work with seat belts. They do not provide full protection by themselves.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is better balanced than one with a single rider.
When passing a motorcycle, you must move into the left lane completely.
A motorcycle's brake lights turn on when the motorcyclist slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, you must move into the left lane completely.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Make sure your vehicle is completely in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: You must stay at least ____ behind an emergency vehicle with its siren on.

options.text: One mile
1,000 feet
750 feet
500 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: You must stay 500 feet behind emergency vehicles like ambulances, fire trucks, and police cars when their sirens are on. This keeps the road clear for them.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed through the entire curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve, then gradually speed up as you leave it. Speeding up as you enter makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot around a large truck or vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large truck or vehicle
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is the blind spot around large vehicles like trucks. Avoid staying in these areas where the truck driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Use either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to the right side of the road when there is enough space between your vehicle and the one you passed.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: An upcoming intersection.
Road construction.
An upcoming curve in the road.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when moving left, you should look:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to see your blind spot.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Only know generally where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your route before you start driving. Check a map to find your destination. Don't start a trip with only a vague idea of where you are going.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing without signals?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down at unmarked railroad crossings. Look both ways on all tracks to make sure no trains are coming. If you see or hear a train, stop a safe distance from the tracks and wait until it passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that bicycles may be on or near the road.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed. This helps other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing and prevents crashes.

questions.question: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
If you are on an expressway.
If traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: You may cross the broken yellow line to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: What does the posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe driving speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: The speed limit shows the maximum legal speed for good conditions. You may need to drive slower when conditions are poor, such as in rain, snow, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive above the speed limit.
Decrease your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and large trucks must stop at all railroad crossings. Do not pass within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: A driver ahead is not dimming their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Firmly pump your brakes.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pump the brakes firmly in an emergency. This stops your car quickly and lets you continue steering.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed when driving around curves?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part of the curve.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, throughout, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's inertia makes it harder to turn, so you must reduce speed to stay in control.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again to check for any vehicles you missed.
